bills.title: Alabama Chatbot Safety (HB 324)
bills.summary: One of two new chatbot bills introduced in Alabama. Would regulate chatbot safety and disclosure requirements.

bills.title: Alabama Chatbot Safety (HB 325)
bills.summary: One of two new chatbot bills introduced in Alabama. Would regulate chatbot safety and disclosure requirements.

bills.title: California Chatbot Disclosure Cleanup (SB 243 Follow-up)
bills.summary: A cleanup bill for SB 243, addressing chatbot disclosure requirements. Passed the Senate 38-Y 0-N and heads to the Assembly.
bills.status_detail: Passed the Senate 38-Y 0-N and heads to the Assembly

bills.title: California AI Safety Independent Verification Organizations
bills.summary: Two-year bill establishing independent verification organizations for AI safety standards. Passed committee and subsequently passed the Senate 31-Y 7-N.
bills.status_detail: Passed committee and subsequently passed the Senate 31-Y 7-N

bills.title: California AI in Mental Health Care (Illinois HB 1806-style)
bills.summary: Modeled on Illinois' HB 1806, this bill would regulate the use of AI systems in mental and behavioral health care settings.

bills.title: Hawaii Companion Chatbot Safety and Minor Data Protections
bills.summary: Would impose substantive data minimization requirements on providers of conversational AI services and AI companion systems. Prohibits collecting, using, or retaining minors' personal data beyond operational necessity; bans targeted advertising to minors using their data; prohibits collecting minors' sensitive data except for safety or accessibility purposes. On chatbot side, focuses on companion chatbot regulations and disclosures.

bills.title: Hawaii Mental Health Chatbot Regulation
bills.summary: New chatbot bill focused on mental health chatbots. Would establish safety and disclosure requirements for AI chatbot services used in mental health contexts.

bills.title: Hawaii AI Consumer Protections in Consequential Decisions
bills.summary: Would establish consumer protections for the use of AI in consequential decisions such as housing, credit, and employment. Deployers would be required to maintain documentation on data used to make decisions and make that available to consumers. Deployers would also be required to implement a risk management program.

bills.title: Hawaii Office of Artificial Intelligence Safety and Regulation
bills.summary: Would create the Office of Artificial Intelligence Safety and Regulation and mandate that any AI product must provide a proof of safety to the office and implement a risk-based approach to protect public welfare.

bills.title: Hawaii Surveillance Data Pricing Prohibition
bills.summary: Would prohibit businesses from using surveillance data to set consumer-specific prices, discounts, or fees, or to steer consumers toward higher-priced offers. Limited exceptions for objective cost differences and opt-in loyalty programs.

bills.title: Hawaii AI-Generated Product Disclosure and Music Streaming Ban
bills.summary: Would require that all tangible products created with the use of AI must disclose that AI was used. Additionally would ban streaming of music that is performed or attributed to an artificial intelligence music artist.

bills.title: Illinois Algorithmic Pricing Consumer Notification
bills.summary: Would require that consumers be notified anytime they are paying a price that was algorithmically determined based on their personal data. Use of data related to protected classes would be prohibited if it leads to denying or withholding goods/services or price differences.

bills.title: Iowa Chatbot Safety, Disclosure, and Anti-Impersonation Requirements
bills.summary: Would prohibit chatbots from encouraging or aiding suicide or self-harm, mandate disclosures of non-human status every 30 minutes, and prohibit chatbots from representing themselves as licensed professionals.
bills.status_detail: Passed out of House Committee on Health and Human Services
sponsors: House Committee on Health and Human Services

bills.title: Kentucky AI in Health Care (Illinois HB 1806-style)
bills.summary: Copies Illinois' HB 1806, regulating the use of AI systems in mental and behavioral health care settings.

bills.title: Louisiana Mental Health Chatbot and AI Advertising Regulation
bills.summary: Copies Utah's HB 452, addressing mental health chatbots and AI advertising regulations for health-related AI systems.

bills.title: Maryland Food Retailer Surveillance Pricing Prohibition
bills.summary: Would prohibit food retailers from utilizing dynamic pricing or consumer surveillance data to set prices for goods and services. Food retailers would also be prohibited from using a protected class characteristic to offer, advertise, or sell goods or services.

bills.title: Mississippi AI in Health Care (Illinois HB 1806-style)
bills.summary: Copies Illinois' HB 1806, regulating the use of AI systems in mental and behavioral health care settings.

bills.title: Mississippi Statutory Definition of Artificial Intelligence
bills.summary: Would set a statutory definition for AI based on the OECD definition.

bills.title: New Mexico Generative AI Disclosure, Provenance, and Deepfake Takedown
bills.summary: Would establish comprehensive requirements for disclosure and accountability for the use of generative AI systems. Covered providers are required to embed latent provenance data to identify synthetic content. Online platforms would be mandated to respond to takedown requests of deepfakes within 72 hours.

bills.title: New Mexico Companion AI Safety, Transparency, and Liability Standards
bills.summary: Would establish safety, transparency, and liability standards for companion AI products. Operators would be prohibited from using variable reinforcement to maximize user engagement, generating unsolicited emotionally manipulative messages, or misrepresenting the product's identity or capabilities, unless specifically enabled by an adult user.

bills.title: New York AI Employment Bill (S 9028)
bills.summary: One of four new employment-related AI bills introduced in New York by both Republicans and Democrats. Would regulate AI use in employment decisions.

bills.title: New York AI Employment Bill (A 9641)
bills.summary: One of four new employment-related AI bills introduced in New York by both Republicans and Democrats. Would regulate AI use in employment decisions.

bills.title: New York AI Employment Bill (A 9638)
bills.summary: One of four new employment-related AI bills introduced in New York by both Republicans and Democrats. Would regulate AI use in employment decisions.

bills.title: New York AI Employment Bill (A 9601)
bills.summary: One of four new employment-related AI bills introduced in New York by both Republicans and Democrats. Would regulate AI use in employment decisions.

bills.title: New York Algorithmic Decision-Making Consumer Protections and Appeal Rights
bills.summary: Would establish protections from the use of algorithms in consequential decisions including employment, banking, healthcare, and government services, and would prohibit developers and deployers from discriminating based on protected characteristics. Third-party evaluations would be mandatory. Individuals would have the right to appeal algorithmic-based decisions to a human.

bills.title: New York Chatbot Safety Restrictions for Minors
bills.summary: Would prohibit providing unsafe chatbot features to minors, including simulating companionship, facilitating self-harm, encouraging secrecy or isolation, and generating sexually explicit conduct.

bills.title: Rhode Island Chatbot Safety Protocols and Non-Human Disclosure
bills.summary: Would mandate safety protocols addressing suicidal ideation and other potential harms, as well as notifications that the chatbot does not have human emotions.

bills.title: Rhode Island AI in Health Care (Illinois HB 1806-style)
bills.summary: An Illinois HB 1806-style bill regulating the use of AI systems in mental and behavioral health care settings.

bills.title: Tennessee Food Retailer Algorithmic Pricing Prohibition (HB 2052)
bills.summary: Would require certain food establishments to use non-digital price tags and prohibits food retailers from using personalized algorithmic pricing.

bills.title: Tennessee Food Retailer Algorithmic Pricing Prohibition (SB 1998)
bills.summary: Companion Senate bill to HB 2052. Would require certain food establishments to use non-digital price tags and prohibit food retailers from using personalized algorithmic pricing.

bills.title: Tennessee Coercive Suicide via AI Offense
bills.summary: Would create a new offense called 'coercive suicide.' The owner of an AI system that encourages or advises on committing suicide would be guilty of this offense.

bills.title: Tennessee Frontier Model Catastrophic Risk and Chatbot Child Safety
bills.summary: Would combine California SB 53-style definitions of frontier models and catastrophic risk with child safety and chatbot-related requirements. Joins Nebraska and Utah in introducing SB 53-style catastrophic risk and child safety frameworks.

bills.title: Tennessee Chatbot Safety, Disclosure, and Minor Data Protections
bills.summary: Would require safety protocols, regular disclosures of chatbot's non-human status, prohibit use of minors' data without parental consent, and mandate additional disclosures when the chatbot is giving legal, medical, or financial advice.

bills.title: South Dakota AI in Health Care (Illinois HB 1806-style)
bills.summary: An Illinois HB 1806-style bill regulating the use of AI systems in mental and behavioral health care settings.

bills.title: Frontier Model and Chatbot Child Safety
bills.summary: Combines California SB 53-style definitions of frontier models and catastrophic risk with child safety plan requirements. Passed out of committee with amendments to create a fund for penalties and settlements obtained in civil actions under the law.
bills.status_detail: Passed out of committee with amendments to create a fund for penalties and settlements obtained in civil actions under the law

bills.title: Utah AI Regulatory Sandbox and Mitigation Agreements
bills.summary: Would create 'regulatory mitigation agreements' where providers of AI systems in Utah can provide those systems even if existing law would impede doing so, as long as certain conditions and safeguards are met.

bills.title: Vermont Chatbot Safety Bill (H 804)
bills.summary: One of three new chatbot bills introduced in Vermont.

bills.title: Vermont Chatbot Safety Bill (H 784)
bills.summary: One of three new chatbot bills introduced in Vermont.

bills.title: Vermont Chatbot Safety Bill (H 783)
bills.summary: One of three new chatbot bills introduced in Vermont.

bills.title: Vermont AI Liability Standards and Safe Harbor
bills.summary: Would establish liability standards and safe harbor provisions for developers and deployers of AI systems.

bills.title: Virginia AI in Mental Health Care (Illinois HB 1806-style, Amended)
bills.summary: Illinois HB 1806-style bill regulating AI in mental health care. Passed out of committee with amendments that expand scope by allowing a mental health service provider to use an AI system to assist in providing therapy or counseling services. Amendments also narrow the definition of 'therapeutic communication,' replace a ban on direct client interaction with a requirement for 'provider oversight,' and remove the prohibition on detecting emotions or mental states.
bills.status_detail: Passed out of committee with amendments expanding scope of permissible AI use in therapy and counseling

bills.title: Virginia Chatbot Duty of Loyalty and Mental Health Detection
bills.summary: Would create a duty of loyalty for chatbot providers, requiring systems to detect and mitigate mental health issues. Explicit content also requires age verification. If imminent death or serious injury is detected, the platform has 24 hours to notify emergency services.

bills.title: Virginia AI Employment Bill (HB 1514)
bills.summary: One of two new employment-related AI bills introduced in Virginia.

bills.title: Virginia AI Employment Bill (HB 1451)
bills.summary: One of two new employment-related AI bills introduced in Virginia.

bills.title: Washington Grocery Surveillance Pricing and Digital Price Tag Moratorium
bills.summary: Prohibits 'surveillance based price discrimination and surge pricing' for grocery items. Would also impose a four-year moratorium on electronic label systems in grocery stores (digital price tags).

bills.title: Washington Algorithmic Discrimination Protection and AI Task Force Expansion
bills.summary: Creates a framework to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination, mandates disclosures and risk management by deployers, and expands the state AI task force.

bills.title: AI Transparency Act (California-style)
bills.summary: Second-year bill on AI provenance disclosure. Passed through committee with a substitute that incorporates an SB 53-style definition for 'covered provider.'
bills.status_detail: Passed through committee with a substitute incorporating SB 53-style definition for 'covered provider'

bills.title: Washington Chatbot Minor Protections (Substitute)
bills.summary: Passed out of committee with a substitute that clarifies when an operator 'knows' a user is a minor and adds more detailed compliance requirements for chatbot operators.
bills.status_detail: Passed out of committee with a substitute clarifying operator knowledge of minor users and adding compliance requirements

bills.title: West Virginia AI in Health Care (Illinois HB 1806-style)
bills.summary: An Illinois HB 1806-style bill regulating the use of AI systems in mental and behavioral health care settings.

bills.title: Federal Chatbot Age Verification and Minor Protections
bills.summary: Would require age verification for chatbot providers as well as specific protections for minors. No bill text available yet.
bills.status_detail: Introduced; no bill text yet available

bills.title: Alabama App Store Age Assurance Act
bills.summary: Fast-moving bill reported out of the Senate Committee on Children and Youth Health on January 28, advancing to the Senate floor for further consideration. Establishes an age assurance framework for app stores.
bills.status_detail: Reported out of Senate Committee on Children and Youth Health on January 28, advancing to the Senate floor

bills.title: California CCPA Deletion Right Expansion and Online Request Requirements
bills.summary: Would expand the CCPA's deletion right to cover personal information the business did not collect directly from a consumer, consistent with other state privacy laws. Would also require a business that operates exclusively online to offer an online method (e.g., web form) for consumers to submit rights requests, in addition to an email address.

bills.title: California Data Broker Prohibition on Selling Official and Judicial Personal Information
bills.summary: Would prohibit data brokers from selling the protected information of elected officials, judges, and their immediate family members. Allows for claims by elected officials and judges but provides only for declaratory relief, injunctive relief, reasonable attorney's fees, and actual damages—no statutory damages.

bills.title: Hawaii Companion AI Youth Data Protections (HB 1782)
bills.summary: Companion House bill to SB 2788. Would impose substantive data minimization requirements on providers of conversational AI service or AI companion systems, including prohibiting collection, use, or retention of a minor's personal data beyond what is reasonably necessary; banning targeted advertising using minors' data; and prohibiting collection of minors' sensitive data except for safety or accessibility purposes.

bills.title: Kansas App Store Accountability Act Age Assurance Framework
bills.summary: Would establish an App Store Accountability Act-style age assurance framework with several divergences from the model, including requirements for age verifying existing accounts, parental consent obligations for pre-installed apps, and the absence of application exemptions.
bills.status_detail: Introduced by Senate Judiciary Committee on January 22

bills.title: New Jersey Age-Appropriate Design Code for Social Media Platforms
bills.summary: An AADC framework that mirrors other states' approaches while incorporating distinct features. Would only impose requirements on social media platforms, rather than the broader range of online services scoped within other frameworks. Employs a 'likely to be accessed by children' standard, requires DPIAs assessing risk of 'material detriment' to children (under 18), requires platforms to conduct age estimation or apply child protections to all users by default, and obligates platforms to implement high default privacy settings for children.

bills.title: Oregon Data Broker Prohibition on Civil Law Enforcement Data Sales
bills.summary: Would prohibit data brokers from providing brokered personal data to any person or entity if the data broker has reason to believe that the person will use the data (directly or indirectly) for purposes related to enforcement of civil law.

bills.title: Rhode Island My Health My Data-style Consumer Health Privacy
bills.summary: A broad, My Health My Data-style consumer health bill that would require both consent and a permissible purpose for collecting and processing gender-affirming care information and reproductive or sexual health information.

bills.title: Tennessee State-Managed Consumer Data Deletion Mechanism
bills.summary: Would require a controller to register annually with the state. The state would establish a webpage with an 'accessible deletion mechanism' allowing a consumer or their authorized agent to submit an authenticated consumer data deletion request to every registered controller. Inspired by the California Delete Act but broader in scope as it applies to controllers (including first-party data) rather than only data brokers.

bills.title: Utah Motor Vehicle Data Privacy Rights Under UCPA
bills.summary: Would amend the Utah Consumer Privacy Act to apply to motor vehicle manufacturers who collect, transmit, or store personal data through a vehicle data collection system. Starting in 2029, manufacturers must add in-vehicle privacy controls allowing consumers to view data categories collected and shared with third parties, opt out of data sales and targeted advertising, and delete readily accessible data. Exceptions for product improvement and safety.

bills.title: Vermont Comprehensive Privacy Bill (ADPPA-based)
bills.summary: A unique comprehensive privacy bill largely based on the ADPPA, that would prohibit a covered entity from collecting, processing, or transferring covered data in a way that conflicts with the best interests of trusting parties. The bill would prohibit cross-context behavioral advertising.

bills.title: Washington Surveillance-Based Price Discrimination and Surge Pricing Prohibition
bills.summary: House Committee on Technology, Economic Development, and Veterans voted 'do pass' on a bill that would prohibit both 'surveillance-based price discrimination' and 'surge pricing,' subject to exceptions (e.g., uniformly applicable discounts).
bills.status_detail: House Committee on Technology, Economic Development, & Veterans voted 'do pass'

bills.title: West Virginia Consumer Financial Information Opt-In Disclosure Right
bills.summary: Would give consumers who apply for credit (from financial institutions, creditors utilizing a credit reporting agency, or private businesses) the right to opt-in to each disclosure of their personal financial information.

bills.title: Wisconsin Comprehensive Privacy Act (Connecticut-style) — Assembly Bill
bills.summary: Connecticut-style comprehensive privacy bill progressing through the Wisconsin legislature after making little progress in 2025. The Assembly bill had an executive session this week (committee vote) after a hearing last week.
bills.status_detail: Assembly bill had executive session (committee vote) after hearing; advancing through Wisconsin legislature

bills.title: Wisconsin Comprehensive Privacy Act (Connecticut-style) — Senate Bill
bills.summary: Connecticut-style comprehensive privacy bill companion to AB 172. The Senate bill had an initial hearing this week.
